questions.stem: According to the passage, what is one function of the circadian rhythm?
options: It determines a person's blood type over time.
It governs when people feel sleepy and when they feel more wakeful.
It only controls heart rate and blood pressure.
It causes people to feel hungry at set times each day.
questions.evidence: It governs when we become sleepy and when we are more wakeful.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에 일주기 리듬이 졸림과 각성 시점을 조절한다고 명시되어 있다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as a place that stays on standard time year-round?
options: Hawaii
Puerto Rico
American Samoa
California
questions.evidence: The state of Hawaii and most of the state of Arizona do not make the spring change. Those areas remain on standard time along with Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에는 하와이, 애리조나, 푸에르토리코, 아메리칸사모아, 괌, 미국령 버진아일랜드만 언급되며 캘리포니아는 언급되지 않는다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the passage about why teenagers become 'hard-to-wake'?
options: Teenagers naturally require less sleep than young children.
Circadian rhythms shift with age, causing teens to prefer waking later.
Teenagers are more affected by daylight saving time than adults.
Young children have a stronger circadian rhythm than teenagers.
questions.evidence: The rhythms change with age. This is one reason that early-to-rise young children turn into hard-to-wake teenagers.
questions.explanation_ko: 리듬이 나이에 따라 변한다는 문장에서 청소년기에 리듬이 늦게 맞춰진다는 것을 추론할 수 있다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the study of U.S. traffic deaths?
options: To argue that daylight saving time should be abolished immediately.
To show a real-world danger linked to sleep deprivation after the time change.
To compare car accident rates between Hawaii and Arizona.
To explain how melatonin levels affect driving ability.
questions.evidence: Deadly car crash numbers increase the first few days after the spring time change, a study of U.S. traffic deaths says.
questions.explanation_ko: 저자는 수면 부족이 실제로 위험한 결과(교통사고 증가)를 초래한다는 것을 보여주기 위해 이 연구를 언급한다.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'However, there are ways to ease the effects of the time change,' the word 'ease' most nearly means:
options: to increase
to reduce or lessen
to explain
to prevent completely
questions.evidence: However, there are ways to ease the effects of the time change, including getting more sunshine.

blanks.sentence_ko: 미국의 많은 지역은 3월 9일 일요일에 서머타임을 위해 '시간을 앞으로 당긴다'.
하지만 시간 변화의 영향을 완화할 방법들이 있는데, 그중 하나는 햇빛을 더 많이 쬐는 것이다.
그 빛은 건강한 수면을 위해 당신의 일주기 리듬을 재설정하는 데 도움을 준다.
하지만 미국 성인의 3분의 1이 이미 권장되는 7시간의 밤잠을 자지 못하고 있어서, 부족한 잠을 보충하는 것은 어려울 수 있다.
이미 위험에 처한 사람들에게서 고혈압과 같은 다른 문제에 갑작스러운 일주기 변화가 영향을 미칠 가능성이 있다.

key_points: Daylight saving time can disrupt the body's circadian rhythm, which governs sleep and wakefulness.
The spring time change is linked to increased heart attacks, strokes, and traffic accidents in the days that follow.
Some U.S. states and territories, like Hawaii and Arizona, do not observe daylight saving time.
Experts recommend gradually shifting bedtime earlier and getting morning sunlight to ease the transition.
Health organizations such as the American Medical Association support ending time changes in favor of permanent standard time.
main_idea: Daylight saving time disrupts the body's circadian rhythm and is linked to health risks, so experts recommend gradual adjustment strategies and some groups favor ending the practice altogether.
restate_sentence: Too much light in the evening — that extra hour from daylight saving time — delays the melatonin increase.
